proposedTopics.title: Trees
proposedTopics.description: Recursive/hierarchical structure. Iterative traversal reuses Stack; construction/pointer rewiring reuses Linked List concepts.

proposedTopics.title: DFS traversals
proposedTopics.description: Recurse (or use an explicit stack) into children before returning, in pre/in/post order. This is the base traversal every other tree pattern builds on. Recognize: "visit every node", ordered output of a BST via inorder.

proposedTopics.title: BFS / level-order traversal
proposedTopics.description: A queue processes nodes level by level, tracking level boundaries by queue-size snapshots. Recognize: "per-level" output, shortest path in an unweighted tree/grid-as-tree.

proposedTopics.title: BST validation
proposedTopics.description: Carry a valid (low, high) range down the recursion, tightening it at each step, instead of only comparing to immediate children. Recognize: "is this a valid BST", BST-specific search/insert/delete.

proposedTopics.title: Lowest common ancestor
proposedTopics.description: Recurse into both subtrees; a node is the LCA when the target lives in different subtrees (or is the node itself). BST version uses value comparisons instead of full search. Recognize: "lowest common ancestor of two nodes".

proposedTopics.title: Tree construction from traversals
proposedTopics.description: Use one traversal to find the root/split point and another to recurse into left/right subtrees, typically with a hash map for O(1) index lookup. Recognize: "build tree from preorder+inorder", "build from sorted array".

proposedTopics.title: Path-sum patterns
proposedTopics.description: Carry a running value (sum, max, or path list) down the recursion and combine child results on the way back up. Recognize: root-to-leaf accumulation, "diameter/longest path", "max path sum through any node".

proposedTopics.title: Serialization/deserialization
proposedTopics.description: Encode a tree to a string via a traversal that marks null children explicitly, then rebuild by consuming that string in the same traversal order. Recognize: "design serialize/deserialize", tree-to-string round-trip.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a DFS tree traversal, and how do preorder, inorder, and postorder differ? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "visit every node", and the position of the node-visit relative to its children fixes the order — preorder (node before children) copies/serializes top-down, inorder (left, node, right) emits a BST in sorted order, postorder (children before node) frees/aggregates bottom-up; pitfall: forgetting the null-child base case and dereferencing a leaf's missing child. Related: Binary Tree Preorder/Postorder Traversal.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write an iterative inorder traversal with an explicit stack in your language of choice: given a binary tree root, return its node values in inorder.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Loop with a current pointer and a stack: while current is non-null push it and go left; otherwise pop, emit that node's value, and set current to its right child. Invariant: the stack holds exactly the unvisited ancestors whose right subtrees are still pending.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal (Easy) — return the inorder sequence of a binary tree's node values.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Recurse left, emit the node, recurse right — or run the explicit-stack loop to avoid recursion.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree (Easy) — return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A node's depth is 1 plus the larger of its two subtree depths, with a null child contributing 0.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for BFS / level-order traversal? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "per-level" grouping, shortest hop-count in an unweighted tree or grid; pitfall: reading the queue length inside the level loop after you have already enqueued children — snapshot the level size once before draining it. Related: Average of Levels in Binary Tree.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a level-order BFS with per-level grouping in your language of choice: given a binary tree root, return a list of levels, each a list of values.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Seed a queue with the root, then repeat: snapshot the current queue size as this level's width, dequeue exactly that many nodes emitting their values and enqueuing their non-null children. Invariant: at the top of each iteration the queue holds exactly one full level.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (Medium) — return node values grouped level by level, top to bottom.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: BFS with a size snapshot per level so each inner loop drains exactly one level into its own list.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Binary Tree Right Side View (Medium) — return the values visible from the right, top to bottom.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Run level-order BFS and keep the last node of each level (the rightmost).

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for range-carrying BST validation? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "is this a valid BST", or any BST search/insert/delete that leans on the ordering invariant; pitfall: comparing only against a node's immediate parent instead of carrying a tightening (low, high) bound — a deep node can satisfy its parent yet violate a distant ancestor. Related: Insert into a BST, Delete Node in a BST.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write range-carrying BST validation in your language of choice: return whether a binary tree satisfies the BST ordering.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Recurse with an open interval (low, high) starting at (-inf, +inf): each node must lie strictly inside, then recurse left with high tightened to the node's value and right with low tightened to it. Invariant: every node is checked against the full ancestor-derived bound, not just its parent.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Validate Binary Search Tree (Medium) — return whether the tree is a valid BST.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Carry a (low, high) bound down the recursion, tightening one side at each step.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Kth Smallest Element in a BST (Medium) — return the k-th smallest value in the tree.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Inorder traversal yields values in sorted order, so stop at the k-th emitted node.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for the lowest-common-ancestor recursion? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "lowest common ancestor of two nodes", the split-point where two root-to-node paths diverge; pitfall: on a plain binary tree, returning eagerly on the first target found instead of letting both subtree searches report back — the LCA is the node where the two targets surface in different subtrees. Related: the BST variant just walks down comparing values.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the lowest-common-ancestor recursion for a binary tree in your language of choice: given the root and two target nodes, return their LCA.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Return the node itself if it is null or equals either target, otherwise recurse both sides; if both sides come back non-null the current node is the LCA, else bubble up whichever side was non-null. Invariant: a call returns a target it saw, or the LCA once both targets have been seen below it.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree (Medium) — return the LCA of two nodes in a BST.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Walk down from the root; the first node whose value sits between (or equals) the two targets is the LCA.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree (Medium) — return the LCA of two nodes in a general binary tree.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Recurse both subtrees; the node whose left and right searches each surface one target is the LCA.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for splitting traversals to reconstruct a tree? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "build the tree from preorder+inorder" (or postorder+inorder, or a sorted array); pitfall: rescanning inorder for the root each recursion (O(n^2)) instead of pre-hashing value->index, plus off-by-one slicing of the left/right subarrays. Related: Convert Sorted Array to BST picks the middle element as the root.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write preorder+inorder tree construction in your language of choice: given both traversals, rebuild the binary tree.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Consume preorder left-to-right as the stream of roots; for each root find its index in inorder via a prehashed value->index map to size the left and right subtrees, and recurse left before right so the preorder cursor advances correctly. Invariant: the preorder pointer always sits on the next subtree's root.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal (Medium) — rebuild the tree from its two traversals.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Preorder gives the root order; each root's position in inorder splits the remaining nodes into its left and right subtrees.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree (Easy) — build a height-balanced BST from a sorted array.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Pick the middle element as the root and recurse on the two halves so the tree stays balanced.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for the down-carry-plus-combine-on-return path-sum recursion? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: root-to-leaf accumulation, "diameter/longest path", "max path sum through any node"; pitfall: conflating the value you carry DOWN (a running prefix) with the value you return UP (the best completed path), and, for through-node problems, forgetting to clamp negative child contributions to zero. Related: Path Sum II collects the actual root-to-leaf paths.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the combine-on-return path recursion in your language of choice: return the diameter (longest edge count between any two nodes) of a binary tree.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A helper returns each node's height (edges down to its deepest leaf); at every node update a global best with leftHeight + rightHeight (the path bending through this node), then return 1 + max(left, right). Invariant: the returned value is a downward height while the answer tracks the best two-sided join seen.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Path Sum (Easy) — return whether some root-to-leaf path sums to a target value.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Carry the remaining target down the recursion; at a leaf check whether its value finishes the sum exactly.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Diameter of Binary Tree (Easy) — return the length of the longest path between any two nodes.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: At each node the candidate diameter is left height + right height; track the max while the recursion returns heights.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (Hard) — return the maximum sum of any node-to-node path.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Each node returns its best single downward branch with negatives clamped to zero, while a global max records the best left + node + right join.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for null-marked traversal serialization? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "design serialize/deserialize", any tree-to-string round-trip; pitfall: omitting explicit null markers (the string can then no longer distinguish different tree shapes) or dropping the delimiter when values are multi-digit or negative. Related: Serialize and Deserialize N-ary Tree, which needs a child-count marker (premium-skip).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write preorder serialize/deserialize with explicit null markers in your language of choice: encode a binary tree to a string and rebuild it.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Serialize by preorder-emitting each value (or a sentinel like '#' for null) into a delimited string; deserialize by consuming that stream left-to-right, building a node from the next token and recursing to fill its left then right child. Invariant: encode and decode walk the nodes in identical order so the cursor never desyncs.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree (Hard) — design methods to encode a tree to a string and decode it back.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Preorder with an explicit null marker for each missing child makes the string unambiguous and lets decode rebuild by consuming tokens in the same order.
